extracted.intended_audience: USPTO OPQA reviewers and patent examiners performing MRF compliance reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Structured quality-review checklist for evaluating whether office-action rejections under 35 U.S.C. (e.g., §112(d), §101 subject-matter/utility, statutory double patenting) comply with statutory and USPTO guidance; includes required checkboxes, explanatory guidance, characteristics, and accolade rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer write-up tone and personalization
rubrics_metrics.description: The write up should avoid rhetorical questioning. The write up should not be personalized, but an assessment of the work product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only include objective assessment directed to the work product. Avoid rhetorical questions and personal comments about the examiner. This requirement repeats for multiple statute sections and applies to explanation comment boxes (e.g., Explanation of noncompliance, lack of sufficient evidence).

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(d) Rejection(s) compliance determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Were all the 35 USC 112(d) Rejection(s) in compliance? (Yes or No)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determination of compliance is based on the rejection properly identifying the claim(s), the statute and being supported by sufficient evidence to support the rejection. If a 112(d) rejection was made, the reviewer must answer Yes or No and, if No, continue through the question set to identify the noncompliance basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(d) Identify claim(s) and type of claim causing noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the claim(s) with non-compliant 35 USC 112(d) rejection(s). The noncompliance is directed to limitations introduced in (check only one): Only the independent claim(s) / Only the dependent claim(s) / Both the independent claim(s) and dependent claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List each claim discussed individually as basis for the noncompliance and those dependent claims that inherit it. Choose the box based on where the limitation that is the basis for noncompliance first appears in the claim tree. Examples illustrate how to pick (independent vs dependent vs both).

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(d) Failure due to lack of sufficient evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection(s) does not provide sufficient evidence to support the rejection (must check at least one of 4(b)(i)-4(b)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If checked, identify whether (i) the rejection does not provide sufficient evidence that the claim(s) does not specify a further limitation of the subject matter of the claim from which it depends, or (ii) the rejection does not provide sufficient evidence that the claim(s) does not include all of the limitations of the claim from which it depends. Explanation comments should be limited to the basis for lack of sufficient evidence and consistent with boxes checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(d) Additional Information/Feedback (root-cause boxes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer should check all of the boxes 5a-d that apply to the noncompliance issue(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boxes include: (a) The rejection(s) should have been made under 35 USC 112(b); (b) The noncompliance is the result of an unreasonable claim interpretation; (c) The rejection(s) was improperly based on the patentable significance of the further limitation; (d) None of the above. Do not guess the root cause; explanation comments must support each box checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(d) Characteristics of 112(d) Rejection(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Check all boxes that apply to characteristics exemplified in the rejections made under 35 USC 112(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characteristics listed include: addresses substantially all claims individually / only groups claims of substantially similar scope (limited claim lumping); sets forth a claim interpretation that points out how the examiner is interpreting the claim/term/phrase; included detailed legal analysis of applicable legal issues and case law; Office action included appropriate suggestions to overcome rejections (not general FP language); None of the above. Guidance: use 'substantially' and 'reasonably' judgment; checking indicates presence of characteristic, not accolade-worthy quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: 112(d) Accolade eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there an accolade related to 112(d) Rejection(s)? (Yes or No)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accolade question only available if all 112(d) rejections were in compliance and 'None of the above' is not checked for characteristics. If available and Yes, reviewer must follow current accolade procedures and complete the required sentence per guidance. If not appropriate, check No.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Subject Matter Eligibility prima facie standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed invention may be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 if it is not directed to one of the four statutory categories (process, machine, manufactures, composition of matter) or if the claim is directed to a judicial exception and the claim as a whole does not include additional limitations amounting to significantly more than the exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the baseline for evaluating 101 subject-matter rejections and informs the compliance checks below.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Subject Matter Eligibility compliance determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Were all the 35 USC 101 Subject Matter Eligibility rejection(s) in compliance? (Yes or No)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination based on whether the rejection properly identifies the claim(s), the statute and is supported by sufficient evidence. Statutory compliance standards and scenarios should be consulted. If No, proceed to subsequent identification and explanation questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Identify claim(s) and type of claim causing noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the claim(s) with non-compliant 35 USC 101 Subject Matter Eligibility rejection(s) and indicate whether the noncompliance is directed to limitations introduced in only independent claims, only dependent claims, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each claim discussed individually as basis for noncompliance must be listed. Selection is based on where the limitation that is the root of noncompliance first appears in the claim tree. Examples illustrate selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Whether another compliant 101 rejection exists
rubrics_metrics.description: For all claims identified as having a noncompliant 101 rejection, was another compliant 101 Subject Matter Eligibility rejection applied? (Yes or No)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If every claim listed as having a noncompliant 101 rejection also has another compliant basis (e.g., a compliant prior-art rejection), answer Yes. If even one claim lacks another compliant basis, answer No. Consult 'MRF In-part Instruction' for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Reasons for noncompliance — 4a: failure to identify claims/statute
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection(s) does not properly identify the rejected claim(s) and/or identify the correct statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check 4(a) when either claim(s) or statute is the basis of noncompliance. Do NOT check 4(a) when the issue is insufficient evidence to support an otherwise-identified rejection (use 4(b)-(e) instead). Do not use 4(a) to raise omitted rejections. Explanation box should be limited to the basis for noncompliance related to identification of claim(s) and/or statute; avoid rhetorical questioning and personalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Reasons for noncompliance — 4b: Step 1 insufficient evidence (characterization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 1: The rejection(s) does not set forth sufficient evidence that the claimed invention is not directed to one of the four statutory categories of invention. If 4(b) is checked, check all of boxes 4bi-4bvii that apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rejection(s) may have characterized the claimed invention as: (i) Transitory Signal/Signal per se; (ii) Software per se; (iii) Human Organism; (iv) Use Claim; (v) Information/data per se; (vi) The rejection does not characterize the claimed invention but merely asserts it is not drawn to a statutory category; (vii) Other. Explanation of noncompliance must be consistent with boxes checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Reasons for noncompliance — 4c: Step 2A Prong One (judicial exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 2A, Prong One: The rejection(s) does not set forth sufficient evidence as to why the claimed invention is directed to a judicial exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 4(c) checked, indicate whether (i) the rejection fails to set forth any judicial exception recited in the claim, or (ii) fails to correctly characterize the judicial exception. If (ii) is checked, at least one of: Product of Nature (fail to assess Markedly Different Characteristics), Law of Nature, Natural Phenomenon (other than products of nature), Abstract Idea — and for Abstract Idea choose categories from 2019 Revised Guidance: (a) Mathematical concept; (b) Certain methods of organizing human activity; (c) Mental process; (d) Tentative Abstract Idea — or indicate improper treatment under Section III(C) of 2019 Guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Reasons for noncompliance — 4d: Step 2A Prong Two (practical application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 2A, Prong Two: The rejection(s) fails to set forth sufficient evidence as to why the claimed invention, as a whole, does not integrate the recited judicial exception into a practical application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If checked, indicate (i) the rejection does not address Step 2A, Prong Two at all, or (ii) it addresses Step 2A, Prong Two but the discussion regarding lack of practical application is insufficient. Explanation comments should support boxes checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Reasons for noncompliance — 4e: Step 2B (inventive concept)
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 2B: The rejection(s) fails to set forth sufficient evidence as to why the claimed invention does not provide an inventive concept (i.e., additional elements do not amount to significantly more than the judicial exception itself).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If 4(e) checked, at least one of: (i) The rejection does not identify the additional element(s) in the claim; (ii) The rejection does not address each of the additional elements in the claim; (iii) The rejection relies on the rationale that the claim simply appends well-understood, routine, conventional activities specified at a high level of generality to the judicial exception but does not support it with an appropriate factual determination in accordance with the Berkheimer Memorandum.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Explanation of noncompliance related to lack of sufficient evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Only comments directed to the basis for the noncompliance based on the failure to provide sufficient evidence should be included in this comment box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer should explain basis for noncompliance related to lack of sufficient evidence and ensure explanation is provided in support of and consistent with the boxes checked under 4(b)-(e). Avoid rhetorical questions and personalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Additional Information/Feedback (root-cause boxes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer should check all boxes 5a-c that apply to the noncompliance issue(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boxes include: (a) The non-compliance is the result of an unreasonable claim interpretation; (b) The rejection is not based on the most current patent examination guidance; (c) None of the above. Comments should support reasoning for each box checked and reviewers should not guess root cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Subject Matter Eligibility Characteristics checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Characteristics of 101 Subject Matter Eligibility Rejection(s) — check all that apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characteristics include: addresses substantially all claims individually and limited claim lumping; provides a thorough explanation identifying each step/prong of 35 USC 101 guidelines with accompanying analysis; sets forth a claim interpretation used for rejection (BRI/special definitions); includes detailed legal analysis and applicable case law/policy; Office action included appropriate suggestions to overcome rejections (not general FP language); None of the above. Use 'substantially' and 'reasonably' to exercise judgment. Checking indicates presence, not accolade-worthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Accolade eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there an accolade related to 101 Subject Matter Eligibility Rejection(s)? (Yes or No)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any 101 rejections were NOT in compliance or 'None of the above' is checked for the characteristics, the accolade question is not available. When available, consult current accolade procedures and guidance documents; if Yes, complete the required sentence per procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Utility prima facie standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed invention may be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 Utility when there is no assertion of a specific and substantial credible utility by the applicant, and the claimed invention does not have readily apparent well-established utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets the standard for evaluating utility rejections in the office action being reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Utility compliance determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Were all the 35 USC 101 Utility rejection(s) in compliance? (Yes or No)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination based on whether the rejection properly identifies the claim(s), the statute/subparagraph, and is supported by sufficient evidence. If No, proceed to identify claims and explain noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Utility identify claim(s) and root-of-noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify claim(s) with non-compliant 101 Utility rejection(s) and indicate whether noncompliance is directed to limitations introduced in only independent claims, only dependent claims, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same selection logic and illustrative examples as for other statute sections: choose based on where the limiting feature originates in claim tree; dependent claims that inherit noncompliance must be listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Utility whether another compliant utility rejection applied
rubrics_metrics.description: For claims identified as having a noncompliant 101 Utility rejection, was another compliant 101 Utility rejection applied? (Yes or No)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An individual claim may be rejected under multiple bases; if every claim listed as noncompliant also has another compliant basis, answer Yes. If any claim lacks such, answer No. Consult MRF In-part Instruction for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Utility Reasons for noncompliance — 4a: failure to identify claims/statute/subparagraph
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection(s) does not properly identify the rejected claim(s) and/or identify the correct statute/subparagraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check 4(a) when claim(s) or statute/subparagraph is the basis of noncompliance. Do NOT use 4(a) when the issue is insufficient evidence (use 4(b)). Do not use 4(a) to raise omitted rejections. Explanation comments should be focused and non-personal.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Utility Reasons for noncompliance — 4b: insufficient evidence of lack of utility
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection(s) does not provide sufficient evidence to support that the claimed invention has no specific and substantial credible utility which has either been asserted by the applicant or would have been readily apparent to one of ordinary skill in the art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation comments should be consistent with boxes checked under 4(b). Avoid rhetorical questions and personalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Utility Additional Information/Feedback (boxes 5a-d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer should check all boxes 5a-d that apply to the noncompliance issue(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boxes include: (a) The rejection(s) was based on an unreasonable claim interpretation; (b) The rejection(s) was based on applicant asserted utility failing to be credible; (c) The rejection(s) was based on lack of applicant asserted utility and failed to consider what would be readily apparent to one of ordinary skill in the art; (d) None of the above. Comments must support the boxes checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Utility Characteristics checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Characteristics of 101 Utility Rejection(s) — check all that apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characteristics include: addresses substantially all claims individually and limited claim lumping; sets forth a claim interpretation used for rejection; included detailed legal analysis of applicable legal issues and case law/policy; Office action included appropriate suggestions to overcome rejections (not general FP language); None of the above.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Utility accolade eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there an accolade related to 101 Utility Rejection(s)? (Yes or No)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Available only if applicable (i.e., rejections were compliant and characteristics allow). If available and Yes, follow current accolade procedures and complete required sentence per guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Statutory Double Patenting prima facie standard
rubrics_metrics.description: A claimed invention may be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 Double Patenting when the claimed invention is directed to the same invention (identical subject matter) that is claimed in a patent or co-pending application which has at least one common inventor, common assignee, common applicant or under a Joint Research Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explains the basis for statutory double-patenting rejections and frames the compliance review.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Statutory Double Patenting basis selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Basis for rejection(s) (check all that apply): Provisional / Nonprovisional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer must indicate whether the rejection is based on a provisional or nonprovisional application/patent as the reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Statutory Double Patenting compliance determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Were all the 35 USC 101 Statutory Double Patenting rejection(s) in compliance? (Yes or No)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determination based on whether the rejection properly identifies the claim(s), the statute and is supported by sufficient evidence. If No, continue to identify claims and the basis for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Statutory Double Patenting identify claim(s) and root-of-noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the claim(s) with non-compliant 35 USC 101 Statutory Double Patenting rejection(s) and whether the noncompliance is directed to limitations introduced in only independent claims, only dependent claims, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same claim-tree selection logic and examples as other sections; list each claim individually and include dependent claims that inherit noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Statutory Double Patenting whether another compliant double-patenting rejection applied
rubrics_metrics.description: For all claims identified as having a noncompliant 101 Statutory Double Patenting rejection, was another compliant 101 statutory double patenting rejection applied? (Yes or No)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If every claim listed as noncompliant also has another compliant basis, answer Yes. Otherwise answer No. Consult MRF In-part Instruction for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Statutory Double Patenting Reasons for noncompliance — 5a: claims/basis identification
rubrics_metrics.description: The rejection(s) does not properly identify the rejected claim(s) and/or identify the correct basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check 5(a) when claim(s) or the basis (e.g., provisional vs nonprovisional) is the cause of noncompliance. Failure to properly identify claims should be raised here. If the issue is an omission (should have been nonstatutory double patenting), raise as omitted rejection rather than checking this box.

rubrics_metrics.name: 101 Statutory Double Patenting Reasons for noncompliance — basis mis-identification (provisional vs nonprovisional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to properly identify basis: If the reviewer believes the examiner improperly made the rejection provisional instead of non-provisional, or vice versa, then box 5(a) should be checked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Box 5(a) should not be checked when the reviewer believes the rejection should have been nonstatutory double patenting; that is a separate omitted-rejection issue.
